scopeNote: Historical premiership profile, not a claim about every later personal opinion. All quiz answers are editorial simulations, not responses supplied by Howard. Brazil-specific wording is interpreted in the analogous Australian institutional context. Anachronistic technologies are cautious extrapolations.

sources.title: National Museum of Australia: John Howard
sources.evidence: National gun reforms after Port Arthur in 1996; Telstra privatisation; WorkChoices in 2006; national water initiatives in 2006–07.

sources.title: National Archives: John Howard
sources.evidence: Entered office through 1996 election; lost government and his own parliamentary seat in 2007.

sources.title: Workplace Relations Amendment (Work Choices) Bill 2005
sources.evidence: Created national workplace relations system, direct employer–employee bargaining and Australian Fair Pay Commission minimum wages/conditions.

sources.title: Northern Territory emergency legislation: introduction
sources.evidence: Howard announced intervention on 21 June 2007, using Commonwealth territories powers for child welfare emergency measures.

sources.title: Museum of Australian Democracy: 1999 republic referendum
sources.evidence: Howard opposed republic proposal and campaigned No while permitting constitutional referendum.

sources.title: Anti-Terrorism Bill (No. 2) 2005 inquiry
sources.evidence: Government bill contained preventive detention, control orders, sedition, ASIO and financial investigation powers; parliamentary inquiry recorded constitutional and liberty concerns.

sources.title: Howard stands by death penalty for terrorists
sources.evidence: Howard said he opposed capital punishment in Australia but accepted execution of Bali bombers under Indonesian law.

sources.title: Parliament: overseas skills recognition, chapter 1
sources.evidence: Migration program expanded from 68,000 in 1997–98 to 110,000 in 2003–04, with policy emphasis on skills. Search-index evidence; full-page tool open failed.

sources.title: Citizenship testing bill overview
sources.evidence: Citizenship test proposed knowledge of Australian history, culture and values, and commitment to Australian way of life.

sources.title: Australian War Memorial: official histories Iraq, Afghanistan and East Timor
sources.evidence: Australian combat involvement began Afghanistan 2001 and Iraq 2003; Australia led multinational INTERFET peacekeeping in East Timor in 1999.

sources.title: DFAT: Australia–United States FTA overview
sources.evidence: Liberalised trade and investment while retaining pharmaceutical benefits, investment screening, audiovisual and quarantine protections.

sources.title: John Howard 2004 campaign speech
sources.evidence: Pledged retention of Medicare safety net, higher GP rebates and subsidies for out-of-hours services, with choice among provider models.

sources.title: Marriage Amendment Bill 2004
sources.evidence: Government legislation defined marriage as man and woman and excluded recognition of overseas same-sex marriages.

sources.title: Federal government to fund chaplains in schools
sources.evidence: Howard announced voluntary school chaplain program for public and private schools; faith chosen by school community, including Islamic and Jewish schools.

sources.title: PM promises swift action on nuclear report
sources.evidence: Howard supported nuclear power as future energy/climate response while acknowledging contemporary cost disadvantage and the need for economic viability.

sources.title: Australian Parliament lifts ban on therapeutic cloning
sources.evidence: Associated Press reported Howard voted against expanding therapeutic cloning, appealing to a moral limit; Parliament passed the bill on conscience votes.

sources.title: Lazarus Rising: publisher description via Google Books
sources.evidence: John Howard autobiography, revised edition of bestselling 2010 political memoir; discusses climate change, terrorism and government.

sources.title: National Archives: 2005 Cabinet papers in context
sources.evidence: WorkChoices sought unified federal system; bibliography identifies John Howard, Lazarus rising: a personal and political autobiography, HarperCollins, Sydney, 2010.

sources.title: Lazarus Rising catalogue
sources.evidence: Records 2010 HarperCollins English edition. No verified Portuguese edition found in dedicated search.

sources.title: National Archives: Howard during office
sources.evidence: Howard government responded militarily to East Timor crisis following 1999 independence plebiscite.

facts: WorkChoices (2005–06) moved employment law towards a national system.
Northern Territory intervention (June 2007) used federal powers against territorial failure.
estrutura.tension: Constitutional federation retained; willingness to centralise named policies does not mean abolition of elected states or local government.

facts: Won government through competitive elections in 1996 and lost it in 2007.
Opposed republic but held 1999 constitutional referendum.
representacao.tension: Constitutional monarchist and representative parliamentarian, not advocate of an executive monarch or permanent unelected ruler; no evidence of enthusiasm for popular assemblies/recall.

facts: 1996 national gun restrictions.
2005 preventive detention and control orders.
2007 rejection of domestic death penalty alongside support for Bali bomber executions.
poder.tension: Security-oriented policy has legal and parliamentary constraints; domestic abolitionism and free political debate should not disappear into an authoritarian stereotype.

facts: Skills-focused migration expanded in the premiership.
2007 citizenship testing emphasised English-compatible integration and Australian civic values.
imigracao.tension: Strict borders and civic assimilation do not imply zero migration, ethnic exclusion or outlawing every immigrant custom.

facts: Combat deployments to Afghanistan 2001 and Iraq 2003.
Led INTERFET 1999.
diplomacia.tension: Willingness to use force and close US alliance differ from unconditional war, independent Australian nuclear weapons or abolishing diplomacy.

facts: Regional leadership through East Timor intervention 1999.
Overseas combat deployments 2001/2003.
intervencao.tension: Alliance-based and sometimes multilateral intervention, not territorial annexation or non-intervention in every conflict.

facts: Telstra privatisation and individual employment bargaining.
2004 campaign pledged Medicare safety net and public subsidies.
economia.tension: Market ownership and private providers coexist with tax-funded public services and welfare; not anarchocapitalism.

facts: WorkChoices strengthened workplace bargaining while retaining a wage-setting commission and minimum conditions.
controle.tension: Deregulation is not elimination of every minimum wage, central bank or stabilisation institution.

facts: AUSFTA effective January 2005 liberalised trade and investment.
comercio.tension: Trade openness retained investment screening, pharmaceutical, audiovisual and quarantine safeguards; no claim of immediate unconditional tariff abolition.

facts: 2006 publicly funded voluntary chaplains, multiple faiths eligible.
religiao.tension: Religious role in education and civic identity coexists with pluralism; no basis for theocracy or replacing civil law with revelation.

facts: 2004 marriage law restricted marriage to heterosexual unions.
2006 therapeutic-cloning expansion opposed on moral grounds.
moral.tension: Traditional marriage/family ethics do not imply criminalising homosexuality or depriving women of employment and political participation.

facts: 2006 advocated nuclear technology as energy/climate response.
2006 opposed therapeutic cloning while allowing conscience vote.
tecnologia.tension: Industrial and technological optimism with bioethical boundaries; no evidence of transhumanism or blanket opposition to scientific medicine.

uncertainties: Scope is historical premiership 1996–2007, not present-day opinions. Retrospective sources only document that period.

Modern questions about AI, cryptocurrency, brain chips, facial recognition and gender language require cautious analogy, not invented direct quotations. Brazilian examples mean comparable Australian institutions or regional circumstances.
